battle.name: 劉裕二次北伐
battle.brief: 義熙五年初春，劉裕再遣大軍北伐北魏，志在河南、河北；拓跋珪自平城率騎南下，兩軍在黃河下游的黎陽、白馬津一線交鋒。前鋒主將劉藩出戰失利而歿，魏騎追至河上，劉裕遣援兵再戰才把魏軍逼退。此役終未能渡河北，卻保住了江南的北面屏障；步卒所恃仍是長矛與大盾，正是斯巴達方陣所用的刺擊長兵。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 這場戰爭發生在東晉義熙五年（409），也就是北魏道武帝拓跋珪的始平元年，交戰地帶在黃河下游的河南、河北接壤處。東晉一方，名義上的君主是晉安帝，實際主持軍國的是都督中外諸軍事、錄尚書事的劉裕：他以鎮軍將軍、揚州刺史之號坐鎮建康，總攬荊、揚、益、寧諸州兵馬，南北兩線的調度皆出其門。劉裕軍的骨幹是他早年從京口、廣陵起家時的老部曲，多是徐州、兗州、青州人，南渡之後又補充了荊、揚兩州的土兵與歸附的僑戶；兵種以步兵為主，輔以騎兵與水軍，糧秣自建康沿淮水、泗水、汴水北運，再由黃河南岸的倉場分發。北魏一方，都城平城，國主拓跋珪在十三年裡平定代人、劉顯、獨孤部與後燕，把塞北諸部收編為八部，以部落兵為骨幹，另徵河洛、冀州一帶的漢人州郡兵與屯田客。魏國立國之本在馬，騎兵是國家軍力最厚的一層，與劉裕以步卒為主、騎兵為輔的體制正好相反。兩個政權的正式關係是敵對與互不相使，邊境上只有掠邊與斷糧的零星衝突，並無穩定的外交條約可依。
countriesEn: This war was fought in the fifth year of Yixi (409), which was the first year of Shiping under the Northern Wei emperor Tuoba Gui, and the ground of contact lay where Henan and Hebei meet along the lower Yellow River. On the Jin side the reigning emperor was Emperor An of Jin, but the man who actually directed the war was Liu Yu, who held the offices of Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs and Recorder of the Secretariat and sat at Jiankang as Governor of Yangzhou and General Who Pacifies the Army; through his hands passed the disposition of the troops of Jing, Yang, Yi and Ning. The backbone of Liu Yu's army was the old command of his own, men from Xuzhou, Yanzhou and Qingzhou who had risen with him in the districts of Jingkou and Guangling, supplemented after the southward migration by the local troops of Jing and Yang and by the households of settled émigré soldiers. Infantry formed the core, with cavalry and river troops in support, and the grain moved north from Jiankang along the Huai, the Si and the Bian, then distributed from the depots on the south bank of the Yellow River. The Northern Wei side had its capital at Pingcheng. Over thirteen years Tuoba Gui had brought down the Daedian, the Liu Xian, the Dugu and the Later Yan, and had organised the tribes of the northern steppe into eight divisions, with tribal troops as the backbone and the Chinese commandery soldiers and tuntian households of the Heluo and Jizhou regions called in besides. The foundation of the Wei state lay in horses, and its cavalry was the thickest layer of its military strength, exactly the reverse of the Liu Yu system in which infantry led and cavalry supported. The formal relation between the two regimes was one of enmity and of neither side maintaining envoys; on the frontier there were only raids and the cutting of supply lines, and no stable diplomatic settlement to appeal to.
people: 劉裕（363—422）自京口起兵，先平桓玄、滅南燕，到義熙初年已把大半個江南握在手中，這次北伐的籌劃出自他手。據《宋書·武帝紀》等書所記，此役先遣中軍將軍劉藩當前鋒；劉藩是劉毅的族子，久隨劉裕征伐，以驍勇見稱。北魏騎兵大舉南下時，劉藩所部先接敵於河上，士卒死傷甚眾，劉藩本人也歿於陣中，軍中為之震動。劉裕在主力尚未集中的情況下另遣援兵趕到，以步騎並進把魏軍逼退，隨後收束兵勢，不再深入。劉裕麾下如檀韶、劉弘之一類北伐宿將亦在此次用兵之列，各家記載對誰領哪一部的說法並不一致。同一時期，劉裕的內部還有一根暗刺：荊州刺史劉毅久鎮揚州，與劉裕爭權，義熙五年劉毅已在暗中布置，義熙七年才起兵作亂，前線的失利與後方的較勁互相牽動。魏國那邊，主帥是道武帝拓跋珪（386—409在位），他以猜忍治國、晚年屢殺大將，內部並不穩定；此役他自平城親率大眾南下，把騎兵壓到黃河一線，是北魏第一次成建制地深入河南。就在這一年二月，拓跋珪被其子拓跋紹所弒，弟拓跋嗣即位，是為魏太宗；弒父與繼位引起的清洗，令北魏在此後數年內無力再南下。
peopleEn: Liu Yu (363-422) rose from Jingkou, put down the Huan Xuan rebellion and destroyed the Southern Yan, and by the early years of Yixi already held most of the south in his hands; the planning of this campaign was his own. According to the annals of the Wu di in the Song shu and other books, the army was first sent forward under the Zhongjun jiangjun Liu Fan as vanguard. Liu Fan was a kinsman of Liu Yi, had served under Liu Yu for long and was noted for his valour. When the Wei cavalry came down in force, Liu Fan's troops met the enemy first on the river, suffered heavy loss, and Liu Fan himself fell on the field, which shook the army. With his main body not yet concentrated, Liu Yu sent a relief force up by another road, and with infantry and cavalry moving together drove the Wei back; he then closed up the lines and did not press on. Veterans of the northern campaigns such as Tan Shao and Liu Hongzhi also served in this deployment, though the records differ on which command each of them held. At the same time there was a hidden thorn inside Liu Yu's own camp: Liu Yi, Governor of Jingzhou and long stationed in Yangzhou, was contending with him for power, and had already begun to make his arrangements in secret in the fifth year of Yixi, rising in open revolt only in the seventh; the reverse in the field and the struggle at home pulled against each other. On the Wei side the commander was the Daowu Emperor Tuoba Gui (on the throne 386-409), who ruled by suspicion and had killed great generals in his later years, so that his own court was far from settled. In this campaign he came south in person from Pingcheng with the mass of his people and pressed his cavalry to the line of the Yellow River, the first time the Northern Wei had advanced into Henan as an organised force. In the second month of that same year Tuoba Gui was killed by his son Tuoba Shao, and his brother Tuoba Si, who succeeded him as the Wei Taizong, took the throne; the purge that followed the murder and the succession left the Northern Wei without the strength to march south again for several years.
kits: 卡面上的斯巴達長矛是希臘人用得最久的一種刺擊長兵：木杆約兩米，槍尾鑲銅套以便落地時不折，槍頭為青銅，作用不在揮砍而在平推與直刺；斯巴達重裝步兵把它握在盾後，列成密集方陣時，槍尖能越過前排肩頭構成一道拒馬般的刃線，靠的正是齊整的步距與不散的陣形。這種兵器與中國步卒手中的矛、槊功能相通，只是材料與形制歷代不同：先秦的青銅矛到漢晉的鐵矛，槍頭日漸狹長而硬；槊則是加重加長、供騎兵與水軍使用的一種。丹陽兵與荊州的雍州兵都以長矛配大盾結陣，盾面多髹漆，其長槍的用途與希臘方陣的長矛如出一轍。除矛槊之外，兩軍的主要裝備還包括弓、弩、環首刀與戟；弩在江南各州的守城與野戰中最被看重，弩機形制自漢末曹魏沿用至南朝，遠射的準頭與重弩可用來對付騎兵。防具上，步兵有札甲與漆木大盾，騎兵有馬鎧與馬具。魏軍幾乎全為騎兵，配角弓、馬槊與長刀，靠的全是馬力與射距；劉裕軍的步卒則以長槊列陣、弩手居後。渡河與野戰所需還有舟筏、蒙沖，以及壘土、鹿角一類的障礙物。
kitsEn: The Spartan dory on the card is the thrusting pole the Greeks used for the longest time: a wooden shaft of about two metres, fitted with a bronze ferrule at the butt so that it would not break when grounded, and a bronze head. Its function was not to cut but to push and to thrust. The Spartan hoplite held it behind his shield, and when the phalanx was drawn up in close order the points rose above the shoulders of the front rank into a bristling line, and what held that line together was the regularity of the pace and the steadiness of the formation. The weapon corresponds in function to the spear and the shao in the hands of Chinese infantry, though the material and the form changed with the ages: from the bronze spear of the early Zhou to the iron spear of the Han and Jin, the head grew longer and harder, while the shao was a heavier and longer form carried by cavalry and by river troops. The soldiers of Danyang and the Yongzhou troops of Jingzhou fought in phalanx of long spears and large shields, the shield faces most often lacquered over, and the function of those long poles was the same as that of the dory in the Greek phalanx. Beside the spears and the shao, the main equipment of both armies included the bow, the crossbow, the ring-pommel sabre and the halberd. The crossbow was the weapon most prized in the Jiangnan provinces for siege work and for field action, the mechanism of the crossbow inherited from the late Han and Cao Wei running on into the Southern dynasties, and its heavy bolts with good sights could be used against horsemen. In the way of protection, the infantry had lamellar armour and lacquered wooden shields, and the cavalry had barding and harness. The Wei army was very nearly cavalry throughout, armed with composite bows, the long mounted spear and the sabre, relying wholly on horse power and on shooting range, while the infantry of Liu Yu formed up with shao spears and crossbowmen behind them. For river crossings and field action there were also boats and pontoons, and such obstructions as earthen works and deer-horn fences.
tactics: 魏軍的戰法是先以騎兵張開，利用平原上速度的優勢在遠距離放箭，消耗南方步卒的陣形與體力，待對方箭矢稍竭、陣腳鬆動，才以數千騎為一隊猛然衝入，撞散步陣，再分成數股追擊潰兵、分割包抄，待主力接應不及再合圍吞掉。劉裕軍的反應是以中軍為核心，把槊盾手排成前後數層、步距緊密的縱深，弩手與弓手居其後，騎兵在兩翼待機，等魏騎衝到近前再以長矛齊出、弩矢覆蓋，把衝鋒擋在陣前；同時以車列與壘土在渡口一線橫向展開，截斷魏騎自黃河北岸的突破口。史料說前鋒失利時劉裕的主力尚在後方，援兵趕到後與魏騎在河上再戰，兩軍拉鋸數日，魏軍因騎兵折損與遠離平城後的補給變長，才掉頭北撤。劉裕軍的另一個難處在後勤：從建康到黃河前沿要經淮、泗、汴幾道水轉陸，距離數千里，軍糧多賴漕運，而黃河下游的春汛與凌汛都會斷航，糧道一旦被魏騎游騎切斷，前線即無以為繼；因此這場仗的勝負手其實不在河上，而在誰能先把糧送到岸邊。兵力的使用上，劉裕沒有把主力一次壓上，而是前鋒先試、援兵次之，說明他對北方騎兵的速度仍存戒心。
tacticsEn: The way the Wei army fought was to spread out with cavalry first and use its speed on the plain to shoot from long range, wearing down the formation and the stamina of the southern infantry; and only when the arrows of the other side had slackened and the line had begun to waver did several thousand riders charge home in a mass, break the formation, then break up into several bands to pursue the fugitives and cut the field apart, closing in to swallow them whole when the main body could not come up in time. The answer of Liu Yu's army was to take the central army as its core and set the shao and shield men in several ranks, one behind the other, with the pace close and the files deep, the crossbowmen and archers behind them and the cavalry waiting on the two flanks; and when the Wei horse came close, the long spears went out together and the bolts of the crossbows fell over the attackers, holding the charge in front of the line. At the same time the carts and earthen works were extended sideways along the line of the fords, so as to cut off the openings by which the Wei cavalry might break through from the north bank of the Yellow River. The records say that when the vanguard was beaten the main body of Liu Yu was still behind, and that the relief force, once it came up, fought the Wei horse again on the river, the two sides pulling at each other for several days, and that only when the Wei had suffered losses among its horses and had lengthened its line of supply away from Pingcheng did it turn about and withdraw north. The other difficulty of Liu Yu's army lay in its rear services: the route from Jiankang to the front on the Yellow River passed by water and then by land across the Huai, the Si and the Bian, a distance of several thousand li, and the military grain came very largely by the transport of boats; the spring floods and the drifting ice on the lower Yellow River could both cut the navigation, and once the supply line was severed by the raiding parties of the Wei horse the front had nothing to live on. The real stake of the battle lay therefore not on the river but at the bank, in who could bring the grain up first. In the use of his troops Liu Yu did not commit his main body in a single push; the vanguard tried the enemy first and the relief followed, and the arrangement shows the caution he still felt about the speed of the northern horsemen.
data: 可以核對的數字並不多。年代最為確定：東晉義熙五年、北魏始平元年，即公元409年，戰役繫於此年正月至二月之間，拓跋珪遇弒也在是年二月。戰場一帶的地理尺度可以估算：黃河自洛陽東北流，至滑縣、黎陽一線轉向，與北魏控制的河北平原隔河相望；劉裕的後方基地洛陽是漢魏舊都，考古測算其城郭周長約二十公里，倉儲、水源與人口都足以支撐大軍屯駐；自建康至洛陽的漕運航程數千里，若全部改走陸路，行程更倍。兵員方面，兩家史書都沒有留下可核實的總數，可以說的是劉裕此役仍是分路出師，前鋒與主力相隔數十以至數百里，實際投入的兵力在數萬量級；魏軍則以輕騎為主，史料多以「數萬騎」形容其突騎之眾，未必是全部兵員。魏騎一日可行數百里，是劉裕最為忌憚的一點——這也是他屍次北伐都無法在河北站住腳的根本原因：南方步卒的行軍速度與戰續力都比不上北方騎兵。往後的對照數字也可排出來：劉裕此後再有一次更深入的北伐，遠抵枳叉、五原一線並修築秦代長城，最終仍因糧道不濟而退兵；北魏道武帝則在同一年二月被弒，繼位的魏太宗在位期間無力南顧，劉裕由此贏得處理內部劉毅之亂的時間。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked are few. The date is the firmest of them: the fifth year of Yixi of the Eastern Jin and the first year of Shiping of the Northern Wei, that is, 409 CE, and the campaign is tied to the first and second months of that year, the murder of Tuoba Gui falling in the second month as well. The scale of the ground can be estimated. The Yellow River flows northeast from Luoyang and turns near the line of Huaxian and Liyang, across the river from the plain of Hebei held by the Northern Wei. The base of Liu Yu was the old capital of the Han and Wei at Luoyang, whose circuit of walls archaeology puts at something on the order of twenty kilometres, and whose granaries, water and population were ample enough to quarter a large army; the water route from Jiankang to Luoyang ran for several thousand li, and the march by land would have been longer still. As for numbers of men, neither history leaves a total that can be verified. What can be said is that Liu Yu again marched in divided columns, the vanguard and the main body separated by scores or hundreds of li, and that the strength actually engaged was in the tens of thousands; the Wei force was light cavalry for the most part, and the records commonly describe its charging riders as several thousand horse, which was not necessarily the whole of it. That the Wei horse could cover several hundred li in a day was the thing Liu Yu feared most, and it is the root reason why none of his northern campaigns could hold a footing in Hebei: the marching speed and the staying power of southern infantry could not match northern horsemen. The later comparison can be laid out as well. Liu Yu campaigned north again more deeply, reaching the line of Zhicha and Wuyuan and building the Qin long wall, and still withdrew because the supply line could not carry it; the Wei Daowu Emperor was murdered in the second month of that same year, and the Wei Taizong who succeeded him could not look south for several years, which gave Liu Yu the time he needed to settle the rebellion of Liu Yi in his own rear.
cause: 打起來的理由，南方與北方各有各的算盤。劉裕這邊最直接：南燕在元興二年（前404）滅亡後，河北與中原的門戶已經打開，劉裕隨即北上修復洛陽的漢魏諸陵，收羅中原士人人心，但他沒有能力立刻吃掉北魏——北魏在平城整合塞北諸部之後，控弦之士數十萬，騎兵來去如風；劉裕必須先把腳下的江南與荊、益穩住，再圖河北。於是他抓住北魏內部不穩這個空隙：拓跋珪晚年多忌好殺，諸將彼此猜疑，平城遠在塞外，調兵遣將都需時日。北魏這邊的理由更簡單：河南是魏的舊疆，劉裕既已修復洛陽、收攏人心，魏就不能坐視南方的政權在舊都立下腳跟；同時魏也想藉南下的騎兵掠取河南的糧食與人口，抵禦柔然。時機上，雙方都選在初春：北方河冰未開、馬匹膘壯，南方陳糧尚可支撐一場短程的進攻。此外還有一層不為人言的權力因素：劉裕與劉毅之爭已到臨界，義熙五年劉毅正在揚州暗中布置，一旦北伐失利或者成功，都會改變他與劉裕之間的力量對比；換言之，這場仗既是國運之爭，也是劉裕在內部壓倒劉毅的一步棋。
causeEn: The reasons for the fighting were the separate calculations of the south and the north. On Liu Yu's side the most immediate was this: with the Southern Yan destroyed in the second year of Yuanxing (404), the gate into Hebei and the Central Plain stood open, and Liu Yu moved north at once to repair the Han and Wei imperial tombs at Luoyang and to gather the hearts of the men of the Central Plain. He had no capacity, however, to swallow the Northern Wei at one stroke, for after the Wei had welded together the tribes of the northern steppe at Pingcheng they had tens of thousands of bowmen and a cavalry that came and went like the wind. Liu Yu had to steady the south, with Jing and Yi, under his feet first, and only then think of Hebei. So he seized on the opening offered by the unsettlement within the Wei: Tuoba Gui in his later years was suspicious and bloodthirsty, his generals were at one another's throats, and Pingcheng lay far beyond the desert, so that every concentration and dispatch of troops cost time. The Wei's reason was plainer. Henan was old Wei territory, and once Liu Yu had repaired Luoyang and gathered the population round it the Wei could not sit still and watch a southern regime set up its foot in the old capital; and the Wei wanted in any case to seize the grain and the people of Henan with the horse that came south, so as to hold off the Rouran. Both sides chose the early spring: the ice on the northern rivers was not yet broken and the horses were in good fettle, while the old grain of the south could still carry a campaign of short duration. There was a further factor that was not spoken of, the question of power: the struggle between Liu Yu and Liu Yi had come to a turning point, and in the fifth year of Yixi Liu Yi was making his arrangements in secret in Yangzhou; whether the northern campaign went badly or well it would shift the balance between the two men. The war was thus a contest of national fortune and at the same time one move of Liu Yu's effort to put down Liu Yi within his own borders.
impact: 此役的結果對雙方的長期走向都留了痕跡。對北魏：道武帝拓跋珪在南下受挫、諸將離心之際被自己的兒子拓跋紹所弒，繼位的魏太宗拓跋嗣清除宗室與權臣，北魏內部經歷一輪重新洗牌，數年之間無力南顧；劉裕正好利用這個空窗期平定揚州的劉毅，收回兵權，隨後把兵鋒轉向荊州的譙縱與盧循，完成了對江南的實控。對劉宋的國策：此役之後，劉裕明白在沒有強大騎兵的情況下，南方政權可以守住河南卻吃不下河北，遂把國策由滅魏轉為守河南、固江南、等北方內變。此後二十年，劉裕、劉義符、劉義隆三朝在北方所做的差不過是修城、屯田、等北魏自己出錯。第三次北伐時劉裕曾遠抵五原、修秦代長城，第四次更一度深入而後全軍而返，說明北方草原的機動力正是南朝無法追平的變數。這一役的另一層作用是心理的：它在北魏人心中確立了南方軍隊並非可以輕易擊敗的對手，此後魏武的南征多為試探而不求決戰；而劉裕雖然在河北一無所獲，卻為半個世紀後的統一預先保住了南方最後的根據地。往後的年表可以排出來：409年拓跋珪遇弒，411年劉毅起兵被平，413年譙縱平滅，415年前後廣州餘部次第廓清，420年劉裕代晉建宋；北魏在439年統一北方，此後又把淮北逐步收去，劉宋在450年前後一度收復洛陽，466年起北魏再盡淮北，479年魏軍南下至瓜步，江北之地幾乎盡失。南北的界線在這七十年裡來回易手，但劉裕守住的那道黃河南岸的防線，始終是南方可以退守的起點。
impactEn: The outcome of this campaign left its mark on the long run of both sides. For the Northern Wei: the Daowu Emperor Tuoba Gui was killed by his own son Tuoba Shao at the moment when his southern offensive had been checked and his generals were drifting apart, and the Wei Taizong Tuoba Si, who succeeded him, purged the clan and the ministers, so that the Northern Wei passed through a reordering of its own and for several years could not look south. Liu Yu used precisely that window to put down Liu Yi in Yangzhou and take back the military command, and then turned his troops against the Zao Yong and the Lu Xun of Jingzhou and completed his effective control of the south. For the policy of the Liu Song: after this campaign Liu Yu understood that without strong cavalry a southern regime could hold Henan but could not swallow Hebei, and he turned the policy of the state from the destruction of the Wei to the holding of Henan, the consolidation of the south, and the waiting for trouble in the north. For the twenty years after that, what the reigns of Liu Yu, Liu Yifu and Liu Yilong did in the north came to little more than building walls, opening tuntian, and waiting for the Northern Wei to make its own mistakes. In the third northern campaign Liu Yu reached as far as Wuyuan and built the Qin long wall, and the fourth went deeper still and then returned with the whole army, which shows that the mobility of the northern steppe was the one variable the southern court could never match. A second effect of this campaign was psychological: it established in the minds of the men of the Wei that the southern army was not an opponent to be beaten lightly, and the campaigns of Wei Wu southward were thereafter probes rather than attempts at a decisive battle. Liu Yu won nothing in Hebei, but he preserved for the south the last of its bases on which the union half a century later was to be built. The later chronology can be set out: 409, Tuoba Gui murdered; 411, Liu Yi rose and was put down; 413, Zao Yong destroyed; by 415 the remaining resistance in Guangzhou had been cleared; 420, Liu Yu took the throne from the Jin; the Northern Wei unified the north in 439 and thereafter took the region north of the Huai piece by piece, the Liu Song recovered Luoyang for a time around 450, the Wei took the north of the Huai again from 466, and in 479 the Wei army came south to the Guabu, so that almost nothing north of the river remained to the southern court. The line between north and south changed hands several times across those seventy years, but the defence of the south bank of the Yellow River that Liu Yu held was always the point from which the south could fall back.
result: 打完了，勝負是可以說的。劉裕的第二次北伐沒有渡過黃河，沒有拿下河北，也沒有實現他在洛陽之外再立一個前進基地的打算；但他保住了從洛陽到滑縣的河南防線，把北魏第一次成建制的南下打了回去，邊界線在這一場之後仍大致維持在黃河一線。前鋒主將劉藩的陣亡是這場仗最直接的代價，魏騎一度追到河上，劉裕的援軍及時趕到才沒有讓全軍崩潰；此後他沒有再試圖第二次強渡，而把主力收回到洛陽與淮泗之間的補給線上。對北魏而言，這場敗績加上同年二月道武帝被弒，幾乎同時抽走了它的進攻能力：拓跋紹弒父奪位，魏太宗在宗室與權臣的清洗中坐穩，數年之間無力再窺河南。於是兩個政權都換了打法：劉裕把主要精力轉向平定劉毅、平滅譙縱與盧循，把江南做成一個可以長期供兵的基地；北魏則把重心放在北方，令太武帝在439年統一北方、然後把兵鋒指向柔然，直到476年拓跋濬暴崩、孝文帝南遷洛陽，才重新把戰線推回南面。從大歷史看，409年的失敗沒有改變劉裕個人的上升軌跡：義熙七年平劉毅，其後平譙縱、廓清廣州，永初元年（420）代晉稱帝，劉宋的江山正是在北伐的失敗裡一寸寸建立起來的。真正被這一役決定下來的，是南北對峙的形態：南方守住了河南，北方守住了河北，兩家的邊界就這樣在黃河兩岸固定了七十年，直到北魏分裂、劉宋趁隙取回淮北，形勢才為之一變。
resultEn: It was over, and the result can be stated. Liu Yu's second northern campaign did not cross the Yellow River, did not take Hebei, and did not achieve what he had set out for, a forward base beyond Luoyang. What it did achieve was the holding of the line of defence from Luoyang to Huaxian, and the turning back of the first organised descent of the Northern Wei; the frontier after this battle still stood in broad outline on the Yellow River. The death of the vanguard commander Liu Fan was the most direct price paid in the fight; the Wei horse came once to the river in pursuit, and only the timely arrival of Liu Yu's relief prevented the whole army from breaking, and after that he made no second attempt at a forced crossing, but drew his main body back to the line of supply between Luoyang and the Huai and Si. For the Northern Wei, this defeat together with the murder of the Daowu Emperor in the second month of the same year drained away its capacity to attack all at once: Tuoba Shao had killed his father to seize the throne, the Wei Taizong sat secure amid the purge of the clan and the ministers, and for several years the Wei could not look toward Henan again. Both regimes therefore changed their method. Liu Yu turned his main effort to putting down Liu Yi, destroying Zao Yong and Lu Xun, and to making the south into a base that could feed an army for a long time; the Wei turned its attention north, brought the north together under the Taiwu Emperor in 439 and then drove the war against the Rouran, and only after the sudden death of Tuoba Jun in 476 and the move of the Xiaowen Emperor south to Luoyang was the front pushed back into the south once more. Seen in the large, the defeat of 409 did not alter the upward line of Liu Yu's own career: Liu Yi was put down in the seventh year of Yixi, Zao Yong was destroyed and the Guangzhou resistance cleared afterwards, and in the first year of Yongchu, 420, he took the throne from the Jin. The state of the Liu Song was built up inch by inch precisely out of the failure of the northern campaigns. What this campaign did settle was the shape of the confrontation between north and south: the south held Henan, the north held Hebei, and the frontier between the two stood fixed on the two banks of the Yellow River for seventy years, until the Northern Wei broke up and the Liu Song took back the north of the Huai in the opening that followed, and only then did the balance change.
